doc.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Monk trio without chords, and the Far North group
summary: A Monk album with Eddie Gomez and Adam Nussbaum, and records with the Scandinavian group Far North, who taught him rubato.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: The idea of having a Monk thing without chords. That was the challenge. Having Gomez was kind of like having chords.
He played Skippy with me in unison. God, I couldn’t believe it. I said, “Eddie, can you do” . . . ? He said sure, and he did. Killer guy.
All sorts of interesting odds and ends, mostly European projects with – obviously for hire projects.

Off the plane and hit. There’s a couple of interesting records with that group we called Far North, with Bobo Stenson, Lars Danielsson, and Jon Christensen. That was a 20-year group, from the mid-’80s – Lars’s initiation, from the mid-’80s to the mid-’90s. We did a live record at Visiones. That was a real fun group. That, I learned a lot, because they definitely played in that style. Bobo and Jon and Lars, those great bass players from Scandinavia. I really enjoyed playing with that group, and that really taught me a
different way to play, because nobody plays rubato like them. They are rubato experts. That’s what they do.
Here’s – I’m looking at one record you did with Lars with the now very popular Nils Petter Molvaer on trumpet.
Yeah, but I think that’s his production record. I just did an overdub.
Yeah, it looks – with an orchestra and all the trappings.
He’s hit some very good stuff in the last few years. He’s hit with success.
